01_bm25.text: Beware of Essential and how it does business. I am extremely disappointed in the Essential PH-1 phone and the company's support model. I bought the PH-1 phone from Amazon who only sells it via third party resellers as Essential the company does not directly sell their phone through Amazon. Within two weeks, the PH-1 camera stops working so I contacted Essential for support. Keep in mind that Essential sells phones but does not have a phone number to contact them for support. They only communicate through email. I describe the problem to them and they request additional information from me: my name, address, proof of purchase, serial number, etc. After providing them with all the data, they inform me that they will not support me because I bought the phone from a reseller. They said they only support the phone if it is bought directly from Essential and Amazon.

This phone is for people that want a company that will support their device and their customers, and not lock it down. This is the first generation Essential PH-1, and there have been weird quirks and bugs, and that's to be expected, but Essential has done what no other modern device manufacturer does: updates and customer service. That in itself is work the price that's half of what you'd pay for another "flagship" device.

This is really impressive. Essential published the December security update at the very same day as Google did for their Pixel 2 phones. No other company did this. And everything looks extremely promising for future updates - The Essential PH-1 has an open Android 8.0 beta test with detailed instructions for manual installation, covered under warranty. Reports say that the software experience is further improved even in the beta version. - The Essential PH-1 will get hardware abstraction layers (HALs) for much easier and faster updates (Project Treble). While all phones that are released with Android 8 or newer are required to implement Treble, phones updated to Android 8 can choose if they want to support it. Essential is one of only three companies that confirmed Treble support. All the big players will not add support to old phones.

I REALLY wanted to love this phone and I do really appreciate the customer support. The U11 guys never responded when I tried to get it fixed. Essential was super helpful right away! That alone is reason to try them again and if they get the hardware right I certainly will. I'm between 2 and 3 stars on this guy: minus 1 for software and minus 2 for hardware but the support was outstanding and I'm going to give this a solid 3. I'm looking forward to a PH-2 review of 5 starts!
And in the end you'll be holding what the Essential PH-1 was always meant to be. A love letter to the industry, now at half the price. Hope this helps! Take care!

If you want a pure Android experience, get this phone!. If you are an Android enthusiast, then this phone is for you. It offers a pure Android experience without annoying bloatware and UI overlays found in do many other devices. Essential has pushed several updates to the platform that has enhanced performance and stability across nearly all aspects of the phone. Hands down the best-designed phone I've ever owned. Migrated to the PH-1 as a former Samsung flagship owner (most recently the S6 Edge), preceded by a Nexus and a Motorola. People close to me have owned iPhones and Samsungs, which I've played around with frequently, so I've had a good sampling of the flagship products for the past several years. I'll say that, unequivocally, the Essential PH-1 is the best-designed phone I've ever owned, by a wide margin. As noted by many others, its industrial design and overall 'feel' is second-to-none. This thing is an absolute joy to use. Once in a blue moon I'm lucky enough to buy something that delights me every time I use it, see it, or pick it up; the PH-1 is exactly such a thing. I read widely about the phone before purchasing it, and the negative reviews made me sufficiently leery to cancel my pre-order.

The camera quality is pretty decent, definitely not as bad as the initial complaints, and for casual use I haven't had any problems with picture quality. The only 2 caveats I have that make this 4 stars instead of a perfect 5 stars are: 1) the signal reception is sometimes weak, and that is arguably the most important part of a phone; and 2) Essential will probably not exist as a company for much longer in their current form, so although they have committed to updates for a while there is still some doubts about their future. The main competitor to the Essential PH-1 that I considered was the OnePlus 6. The Essential PH-1 has not been a disappointment, and I do not regret choosing this phone. It is very good value, especially when it goes for $300 or less.

However, having experienced software/hardware (unsure) issue with the phone that I could not figure out how to solve, the support from the Essential customer service team was courteous, but unhelpful, leaving me with a nice looking brick and in need of a new phone less than 18 months from purchase. The gist of the experienced issue is that phone has shut off after full battery discharge (continuous videoconferencing). After battery was recharged, phone appears to have turned on, but the screen would not, making the phone unusable. After attempting to find a solution on XDA/Reddit on my own, I contacted Essential customer support via chat describing the issue.

I REALLY wanted to love this phone and I do really appreciate the customer support. The U11 guys never responded when I tried to get it fixed. Essential was super helpful right away! That alone is reason to try them again and if they get the hardware right I certainly will. I'm between 2 and 3 stars on this guy: minus 1 for software and minus 2 for hardware but the support was outstanding and I'm going to give this a solid 3. I'm looking forward to a PH-2 review of 5 starts!

Customer support is by email only, and with the issues that arise now and again, it is annoying not to be able to speak with anyone. A gorgeous screen, solid hardware, but it just doesn't do what a top of the line phone should do. I haven't traded out of it yet, but will likely soon.

Zero support. You're on your own.. I've tried contacting Essential's support THREE times in hopes of resolving some problems with the phone. Unfortunately, the only way to get in contact with them is to "request a callback", over which you have no control of the time or date of when they'll call you. Despite requesting a callback THREE times, Essential has not contacted me at all. It's ridiculous. The phone feel nice enough but without support attached to it, it's a worthless device.
The camera is very bad... no optical image stabilization... poor customer support.

Now my phone dismounts my sim card and my carrier is not listed. Contacted support and they tell me and send me the APN settings for my carrier. But it was the same things that is stored in the phone already. Then I was told that my imei number wasn't registered with the carrier. So I contact my carrier and guess what my imei is just fine. So I bought a new SIM to see if that worked... yeah no luck there. So most of the time this phone doesn't keep my carrier activitied. As a whole I'm very disappointed with the customer support. So if you are looking for a phone... I would not look at this one.

Prone to failure and no support or warranty.. I've had 3 of these for about 15 months. One bricked when upgrading to Android P, One had it's fingerprint reader fail after 9 months, and One had it's proximity detector fail ( screen won't turn off when placed next to your face.) For the one that bricked, it took a while to contact Essential customer service, they have no telephone support only email. Even Sprint could not reach them! The replacement phone they sent was CDMA only, the original was CDMA/GSM, so when I switch to AT&T, That phone was useless and since I had Sprint unlock it it's now blacklisted and basically trash. I tried to contact Essential but now no one responds to email anymore. Well there was $500 down the drain. No warranty on any of the 3 phones since no one responds to email and they have no phone or chat help.

And their software issues are getting fixed quickly, but they need to fix the antenna on the next version for sure as numerous people report this problem. I am eagerly following this company to see the next iteration of the device as I will get it for sure.

Essential phone company gives a poor support and not giving any real answers. It took only 3 days for the device to get a boot loop (Neverending boots). (Event recovery menu just boot and cannot be accessed). Essential phone company gives a poor support and not giving any real answers. Now I am stuck abroad without a working phone and no real support. Don't buy this phone poor quality.
Defected product and the worst customer service. The phone was defected and the seller's customer service was not helpful.

Essential refuses to assist customers with defective items. If you are reading this I recommend reconsidering purchasing this device. Everything worked correctly for a few hours, but suddenly the audio from my headphones stopped. I have tried all of the methods I know of to fix strange problems like this. Restarting, a factory reset, developer options, etc. Nothing worked. The speakers on the phone still worked, but using the included adapter did not. I collected a large amount of information regarding the problem I was having and sent it to Essential to see if they could help me. I am not an expert, they should know more. They did not help me at all. They could not confirm if it was the adapter or the phone that was the source of the issue. They did not even try to, perhaps I had already exhausted all the options they would otherwise tell me to attempt.

Decent phone, poor camera, the worst customer service possible.. This phone is a great size and feels very high quality. The camera is quite horrible, and my phone failed 11 months after I bought it. The customer service team takes up to 4 business days to respond to emails so it can take up to a week to send a message, get a reply, and give them the information they seek. I bought this phone in Halo Grey, and spent more money to do it, their replacement phone is going to be black or white and they've told me tough luck that's what we've got when I asked for what else they can do since they couldn't replace like for like.

Horrible support and warranty policies.. I was so excited about this phone, really. The look and feel if the phone is so amazing, the screen is beautiful. I really liked the way it felt in my hand. But that is really where this awesome phone stopped being awesome. I started having issues from moment one, where my signal would go in and out so bad that I wouldn't even get text messages or calls. I couldn't listen to my music. I contacted tech support for the issues and they only work via email by the way, so that took forever. They started having me do tests and change settings on the phone. Every setting and de-bugging report they would want me to do would take another day. I even went and paid for a new sim card to make sure that it wasn't on my end, and it wasn't.

This is really impressive. Essential published the December security update at the very same day as Google did for their Pixel 2 phones. No other company did this. And everything looks extremely promising for future updates - The Essential PH-1 has an open Android 8.0 beta test with detailed instructions for manual installation, covered under warranty. Reports say that the software experience is further improved even in the beta version. - The Essential PH-1 will get hardware abstraction layers (HALs) for much easier and faster updates (Project Treble). While all phones that are released with Android 8 or newer are required to implement Treble, phones updated to Android 8 can choose if they want to support it. Essential is one of only three companies that confirmed Treble support. All the big players will not add support to old phones.

So now I am out of both the phone and partial refund. I am disgusted with both Essential company and Amazon customer service. Amazon used to have great customer service too. Not anymore. I would give a zero for how fragile the phone was and another zero for the customer service from both Essential and Amazon.

Prone to failure and no support or warranty.. I've had 3 of these for about 15 months. One bricked when upgrading to Android P, One had it's fingerprint reader fail after 9 months, and One had it's proximity detector fail ( screen won't turn off when placed next to your face.) For the one that bricked, it took a while to contact Essential customer service, they have no telephone support only email. Even Sprint could not reach them! The replacement phone they sent was CDMA only, the original was CDMA/GSM, so when I switch to AT&T, That phone was useless and since I had Sprint unlock it it's now blacklisted and basically trash. I tried to contact Essential but now no one responds to email anymore. Well there was $500 down the drain. No warranty on any of the 3 phones since no one responds to email and they have no phone or chat help.

This is really impressive. Essential published the December security update at the very same day as Google did for their Pixel 2 phones. No other company did this. And everything looks extremely promising for future updates - The Essential PH-1 has an open Android 8.0 beta test with detailed instructions for manual installation, covered under warranty. Reports say that the software experience is further improved even in the beta version. - The Essential PH-1 will get hardware abstraction layers (HALs) for much easier and faster updates (Project Treble). While all phones that are released with Android 8 or newer are required to implement Treble, phones updated to Android 8 can choose if they want to support it. Essential is one of only three companies that confirmed Treble support. All the big players will not add support to old phones.

Essential phone company gives a poor support and not giving any real answers. It took only 3 days for the device to get a boot loop (Neverending boots). (Event recovery menu just boot and cannot be accessed). Essential phone company gives a poor support and not giving any real answers. Now I am stuck abroad without a working phone and no real support. Don't buy this phone poor quality.

Phone dies in 5 months - no warranty coverage Essential company has no customer support anymore. My phone just died. I bought in August of this year. I cannot contact anyone in essential for warranty coverage.

Do not support a company that won't support their customers.. God awful customer support. Initial impressions were great feel, terribly executed software (very buggy plenty of touchscreen issues, poor memory optimization etc.) We develop mobile applications and firebase shows a crazy skew in crashes on this device (despite having hardly any users on this device). This device is not built to last. Screen began lifting out of the frame, looks like some cheap adhesive (that's why no water resistant certification). This causes light leak on the front facing camera (minor issue) but the lifting screen and gap are a big problem after just a couple months of light use. Customer support had been horrendous - unresponsive, dismissive. Guess they're understaffed and ill equipped to deal with RMAs. What a shame was really rooting for these guys. Shoddy.

Wouldn't turn back on, even to the reset screen (holding down power and volume down buttons). Totally bricked. I contacted Essential, and it was about as good as a customer service experience can be. After trading a couple quick emails with a rep (they wanted to make sure I wasn't an idiot and has actually tried everything), they sent a return shipping label (FedEx overnight), and got me a new phone (brand new, in box) overnighted back. They were quick about every step of the process. I'm not going to knock my 4-star rating, because they handled the issue ideally. Support was perfect.

Originally gave 5 star. The phone is dead less than a year old. A Coworker's phone is also dead. These phones are having a hard time making a year. Build quality seems good. My phone started restarting more and more. Essential customer support will not reply and stand behind the year warranty.

Two stars for the design and build quality ONLY.. Undoubtedly Essential Phone's design and build quality are top-notch. Their support is also good but unfortunately you don't get any actions besides them being (responsive and nice) with their international customers for obvious reasons of Limited Warranty. In a nutshell I can say that I can't recommend this phone to anyone because it just dies after a couple of weeks of using it, LITERALLY! At least that's what happened to my unit. (the picture attached showing the screen while it's ON) Here's my detailed experience if you're interested: It all started in mid-Jan when I got my brand new EP from Amazon. It was all okay with some hiccups every now and then, I knew that before getting it but I believed in Essential team's frequent updates.
We're so disappointed that it has been discontinued, but so impressed that Essential continues to support updates admirably. That is what you call really excellent customer service!

Customer support is by email only, and with the issues that arise now and again, it is annoying not to be able to speak with anyone. A gorgeous screen, solid hardware, but it just doesn't do what a top of the line phone should do. I haven't traded out of it yet, but will likely soon.
